implementation_notes: The platform already ships the factory role: DbProviderFactories.GetFactory("System.Data.SqlClient") returns a DbProviderFactory whose virtual Create* methods (CreateConnection, CreateCommand, CreateDataAdapter) hand out provider-appropriate objects, and providers register the invariant name themselves. The DAO layer is then typed against the abstract DbConnection/DbCommand rather than SqlConnection. Hand-write an abstract DAO factory only when the family spans more than ADO.NET objects, and even then let the provider factory supply the connections while the concrete DAOs keep the SQL.
pitfalls: On .NET (Core), DbProviderFactories is not populated from machine.config; providers must be registered (DbProviderFactories.RegisterFactory or application configuration) or GetFactory throws - typically at startup, which is the good case.
A DbProviderFactory is meant to be created once and reused; creating one per call adds resolution cost and can surface registration errors late.
A provider factory hands out connections, not portable SQL: dialect differences still belong inside the concrete DAOs, and assuming otherwise produces subtly broken queries on the second backend.

variants.name: Keyed services in Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection
variants.implementation_notes: In application code the container is the DAO factory: register one implementation per store under a key (AddKeyedScoped/AddKeyedSingleton, .NET 8+) and let constructors or minimal-API handlers request it with [FromKeyedServices("pg")] or GetRequiredKeyedService; the store key comes from configuration and can be bound per tenant scope. The registration block is the selection table, so keep the key constants in one place to preserve the compile-time-safe part of the pattern; a hand-written factory remains justified only outside a container (libraries, legacy hosts).
pitfalls: Keyed lifetimes must match the store's connection lifetime: a keyed singleton DAO capturing a scoped DbConnection is a captive dependency and leaks one connection to everyone.
String keys resolve at runtime; a typo in GetRequiredKeyedService throws on first resolution rather than at compile time, so centralise keys as constants or a Store enum.
